ledger.x: 697: Venice's tradition dates the first doge, Paolo Lucio Anafesto, and so the state, to 697.
742: the ducal seat moves from Eraclea to Malamocco.
810: the seat moves to Rivo Alto, the core of later Venice.
1000: Pietro II Orseolo's fleet subdues the Adriatic coast.
1030: Ragusa leaves Venetian rule.
Bridging: Croatia-in-union page: 'By 1107 King Coloman controlled most of former Byzantine coastal cities in Dalmatia.'

1116: Croatia-in-union page: 'In 1116, after the death of Coloman, Venice attacked the Dalmatian coast, defeated the army of Croatian Ban Cledin' and 'seized Biograd, Split, Trogir, Sibenik, Zadar and several islands'.
1124: 'Stephen II again attacked the Venetian holdings and regained Biograd, Split, Sibenik and Trogir, but Zadar and the islands remained under Venetian control' (Croatia-in-union page).
1125: 'Doge Domenico Michele reconquered those cities and razed Biograd' (Croatia-in-union page).
1133: Bela II 'won back the lost cities except Zadar' (Croatia-in-union page); Zadar stays Venetian until the loss of 1186.
1186: Zara is no longer Venetian.
1202: Venice recaptures Zara.
1205: Venice occupies Dyrrhachium.
1205: Ragusa is Venetian again.
1205: Venetian troops first occupy Crete.
1207: Genoa's Enrico Pescatore, Count of Malta, holds Crete against Venice.

1207: Treaty of Sapienza page: 'Venice did not appear in the Peloponnese until 1206 or 1207, when a fleet took the Messenian peninsula with the two forts of Modon and Coron from Champlitte's men'; Stato da Mar: 'Methoni (Modon/Modone), 1207-1500 and 1686-1715', 'Koroni (Coron/Corone), 1207-1500 and 1685-1715'.
1207: Corfu comes under Venice for the first time.
1207: Stato da Mar: 'Tinos (Tino), 1207-1715'; 'Paros, Antiparos and Mykonos (Micono), 1207-1537'; 'Feudal lordships held by Venetians, such as Andrea Ghisi in Tinos and Mykonos, are included.'

March 1209: Triarchy page: infobox 'Protectorate of the Republic of Venice (1209-1390)'; Ravano dalle Carceri 'in March 1209 ... signed an alliance with Venice, which recognized Venetian overlordship'.
1212: Pescatore is evicted.
1213: Durazzo leaves Venice.
1214: Corfu leaves Venice until 1386.
1238: Kythira and Antikythera pass to Venice.
ledger.cp: holder not named by the page

ledger.x: 1278: Lemnos leaves Venice.

1291: Patriarchate page: 'In the late 13th century it had occupied the western Istrian coast from Capodistria (Koper) down to Rovigno (Rovinj)' and 'In 1291 a peace was made in Treviso, whereupon the western coast of the peninsula fell to Venice.'
1331: Patriarchate page: 'In 1331 Venice also incorporated Pola (Pula) in the south.'
ledger.cp: holder not named by the page

ledger.x: 1337: Venice conquers the Mestre mainland.
1339: Treviso and Bassano del Grappa are taken: 'followed by Treviso and Bassano del Grappa in 1339'.
1356: Louis I of Hungary's coalition attacks.
18 February 1358: the Treaty of Zadar.
18 February 1358: the Treaty of Zadar, signed at the monastery of St Francis in Zadar, ends the war over Dalmatia.
9 August 1363: the Venetian feudal lords of Crete revolt.
9 May 1364: 'Venice retook Candia'.
1368: the revolt ends.
1386: Corfu becomes Venetian for good: 'Corfu came under permanent Venetian rule in 1386'.
12 December 1388: Maria of Enghien 'sold them to Venice on 12 December in exchange for an annual subsidy of 700 ducats'; the Venetians were 'quickly able to oust Nerio from Nauplia' (Lordship page).
1390: the last triarchs 'left their territories to Venice, which thus established complete predominance over the island' (Triarchy page; the last triarchs died in 1383 and 1390).
1390: infobox 'Colony of the Republic of Venice (1390-1470)'.

22 May 1390: Nerio page: 'On 22 May 1390, the Venetian castellan of Modon and Coron ... met Nerio near Vostitza' and, in the next sentence, 'He ceded Megara to Venice, sent his daughter Francesca as a hostage to Euboea'.
1392: Durazzo returns to Venice.
11 June 1394: 'Argos, Kiveri and Thermisi remained in Theodore's hands until 11 June 1394, when he ceded them to Venice' (Lordship page).
1395: main page: 'In 1481, Venice retook nearby Rovigo, which it had held previously from 1395 to 1438.'
ledger.cp: holder not named by the page

ledger.x: 18 March 1395: the Senate of Venice 'approved his action, acknowledging the annexation of Athens on 18 March 1395' (Antonio I page); Duchy of Athens page: 'From 1395 to 1402 the Venetians briefly controlled the Duchy'; Nerio page: an Ottoman attack 'compelled Donato to cede the city to Venice'.
1396: Scutari is Venetian.

First half of 1402: 'Antonio made a surprise attack against Attica and captured the lower town of Athens'; on 22 August 'the Senate of Venice ordered Francesco Bembo, Bailo of Negroponte, to invade Boeotia' (Antonio I page).
January or February 1403: Antonio 'forced the defenders of the Acropolis to surrender in January or February 1403'.
1403: the Acropolis surrenders; the formal compromise is of 31 March 1405 (Antonio I page).
1404: Vicenza, Belluno and Feltre pass to Venice: 'Vicenza, Belluno, and Feltre were acquired in 1404'.
ledger.cp: holder not named by the page

ledger.x: 1405: 'Padua, Verona, and Este in 1405'.
1405: Ulcinj is Venetian.
ledger.cp: holder not named by the page

ledger.x: 1407: Stato da Mar: 'Nafpaktos (Lepanto): 1390, 1407-1499'.
1408: Patras is Venetian.
1409: Zara returns to Venice by purchase.
1417: Navarino is Venetian.
ledger.cp: holder not named by the page

ledger.x: 1418: Duchy page: 'It officially became a vassal of Venice in 1418 in reaction to the Rise of the Ottoman Empire.'
1420: Venice annexes Friuli.

1420: after the Friuli invasion Venice 'subjected Traù, Spalato, Durazzo, and other Dalmatian cities'; the History page: 'Early 15th century: Venice gained definitive control of the Dalmatian coast from Ladislaus of Naples'.
1420: Cattaro and Perast become Venetian.
ledger.cp: Commune of Kotor (page names no ruler)

ledger.x: September 1423: Andronikos Palaiologos 'handed it over to the Republic of Venice in September 1423' (Siege of Thessalonica page).
1426: Venice acquires Brescia: 'Venice acquired both cities in these years' (Brescia 1426, Bergamo 1428).
1428: Venice acquires Bergamo (see 1426).
1430: Stato da Mar: 'Patras (Patraso/Patrasso), 1408-1430 and 1687-1715'.
29 March 1430: Murad II took it 'by storm on 29 March 1430' (Siege of Thessalonica page).
1438: main page: Venice held Rovigo 'from 1395 to 1438'.

February 1441: Ravenna page: 'The last of the Da Polenta, Ostasio III da Polenta, was ousted by the Republic of Venice in February 1441', and 'the city was annexed to the Venetian territories by the Treaty of Cremona (1441)'.
ledger.cp: Da Polenta lords of Ravenna (page names no state)

ledger.x: 1449: Crema page: 'The seignory passed again to the Visconti, and, from 1449 onwards, to the Republic of Venice.'
ledger.cp: holder not named by the page

ledger.x: 1453: Stato da Mar: 'the Sporades including Skiathos (Sciato), Skopelos (Scopelo), Alonnisos (Alonneso) and Skyros (Sciro), 1207-1270s and 1453-1538'.
ledger.cp: holder not named by the page

ledger.x: 3 April 1463: 'Isa-Beg Ishakovic, governor of the Morea, took Argos by treason.'
1464: Monemvasia is Venetian.
ledger.cp: holder not named by the page

ledger.x: 1464: Lemnos is Venetian again.
1466: 'Cappello's fleet took Imbros, Thasos, and Samothrace.'
10 July 1470: the Ottoman siege of Negroponte begins ('10 July - 5 August 1470').
5 August 1470: Negroponte falls and 'the whole island then came under Ottoman control'.
5 August 1470: the siege of Negroponte ends in Ottoman capture.

1473: 'Cyprus was returned to the Cornaro family and then to the Serenissima' (History page); the 1463-79 war page: Venice recouped its losses 'by the de facto acquisition of the Kingdom of Cyprus in the closing years'.
1474: Mehmed II sends armies against Shkodra and fails; he returns in person in 1478-79.
1479: Lemnos leaves Venice.
1479: bridging.
1479: Zante is Venetian for good.
25 January 1479: 'Venice ceded Shkoder in the Treaty of Constantinople' as a condition of ending the war.
25 January 1479: the Treaty of Constantinople ends the war.
May 1482: the siege of Ficarolo begins (it capitulated on 29 June); the war began 'at the beginning of 1482' over the Venetian visdominio in Ferrara.
17 August 1482: 'Rovigo capitulated to Venice.'
7 August 1484: the Treaty of Bagnolo cedes 'the town of Rovigo and a broad swath of the fertile delta of the Po' to Venice; infobox 'Rovigo ceded to Venice'.
7 August 1484: the Treaty of Bagnolo ends the War of Ferrara.
February 1489: Cyprus becomes a Venetian territory ('In February 1489, the island of Cyprus ...'; the History page: 'Cyprus officially became a Venetian territory (per footnote)').
February 1489: the protectorate becomes annexation.
1499: 'Venice allied itself with Louis XII of France against Milan, gaining Cremona.'
1499: Lepanto falls to the Ottomans.
1500: Modon and Coron fall.
1500: Cephalonia is Venetian.
1501: Navarino is lost.
1501: Durazzo is lost ('Durazzo (Durres): 1392-1501'; the main page lists Durazzo among the bases surrendered after the 1499 war).
1503: Ithaca is Venetian.
1509: Ravenna page: 'Ravenna was then ruled by Venice until 1509, when the region was invaded in the course of the War of the League of Cambrai.'
1509: 'd'Este seized the Polesine', won by Venice in 1484.
14 May 1509: Venice is 'crushingly defeated' at Agnadello; the League of Cambrai had been formed on 10 December 1508.

May 1509: after Agnadello Venice lost 'all the territory that they had accumulated in northern Italy during the previous century'; 'Padua, Verona, and Vicenza were left undefended and surrendered to Maximilian's emissaries'.

14 May 1509 (Agnadello): 'Louis proceeded to occupy Venetian territory as far east as Brescia without encountering any significant resistance'; the page adds that the Venetians 'lost all the territory that they had accumulated in northern Italy'.
17 July 1509: 'Padua revolted in mid-July 1509 and returned to Venetian control on 17 July'; Maximilian lifted the siege on 1 October.
Mid-November 1509: 'Pitigliano recaptured Vicenza'.
1512, before 18 February: Brescia 'had rebelled against the French and garrisoned itself with Venetian troops' (Cambrai page).
18 February 1512: 'Sack of Brescia.
1514: Rovigo page: the Este 'recovered the city during the War of the League of Cambrai', and 'the Venetians, returning in 1514, retained possession until the French Revolution'.
Bridging: no page opened dates the return of Bergamo and Crema (Bergamo, Crema and Brescia pages are silent on 1509-1516).
January 1517: 'Verona surrendered to the Venetians in January 1517, when key treaty provisions took effect'; the war ended with the final truce.
January 1517: the War of the League of Cambrai ends for Venice with the return of Verona (span December 1508 to December 1516 in the lead; the final truce took effect in January 1517).
1520: Brescia page: 'The French occupied Brescia until 1520, when Venetian rule resumed.'
1537: Stato da Mar: 'Paros, Antiparos and Mykonos (Micono), 1207-1537'; Mykonos is the Ghisi lordship the page counts as Venetian (Ottoman fleet, 1537 war).
1537: Duchy page: 'In 1537, it became a tributary of the Ottoman Empire' (infobox 'Ottoman suzerainty: 1537').
1538: the northern Sporades leave Venice.
1540: Nauplia and Monemvasia leave Venice.
3 July 1570: the Ottoman army 'landed unopposed at Salines, near Larnaca' (the fleet sailed on 27 June).
9 September 1570: 'the 15th assault succeeded in breaching the walls' of Nicosia.
1571: Ulcinj leaves Venice.
1 August 1571: Famagusta surrenders after an eleven-month siege and Cyprus is lost; the peace of 7 March 1573 made Cyprus an Ottoman province and Venice paid 300,000 ducats.
1 August 1571: the last Venetian city on Cyprus surrenders (Lepanto, 7 October 1571, changed nothing: 'Cyprus stayed Ottoman' on the main page).
23 June 1645: the Ottoman fleet arrives and lands about 15 miles west of Canea; the Venetians were 'taken by surprise'.
22 August 1645: Chania falls 'after a siege of 56 days'.
20 October 1646: Rethymno falls (its citadel held until 13 November).
1647: in Dalmatia 'Leonardo Foscolo retook Novigrad, captured Klis, and temporarily took the fortress of Knin' (the Ottomans had taken Novigrad on 4 July 1646).

1647-early 1648: Cretan War page: the Ottomans went on 'to conquer the eastern half of the island, except for the fortress of Siteia', and 'By the beginning of 1648 ... all of Crete, except Candia and a few strongholds like the island of Gramvousa, was in Ottoman hands.'
1651: Sitia falls.
8 July 1656: Venetians under Barbado Doer seize Tenedos.
20 August 1656: Venetians seize Lemnos.
31 August 1657: the Ottomans recover Lemnos.
12 November 1657: the Ottomans recover Tenedos.

5 September 1669: Candia surrenders after a siege that began in May 1648; Venice 'kept the Aegean islands of Tinos and Kythera, plus the isolated island fortresses of Spinalonga, Gramvousa and Souda'.
5 September 1669: Candia surrenders; Morosini then concluded a permanent peace on his own initiative.
6 August 1684: Santa Maura (Lefkada) is captured after a 16-day siege; Venice had declared war on 25 April 1684.
11 August 1685: Coron surrenders (its garrison massacred during negotiations), the first Peloponnesian fortress of the Morean War.
11 August 1685: Coron surrenders to Venice.
June 1686: Old Navarino surrenders the day after the 2 June landing, New Navarino on 14 June.
7 July 1686: Modon surrenders.
29 August 1686: Nauplia surrenders, the day Ismail Pasha's attack on the Venetian camp was defeated.
30 September 1686: Sinj falls after failed sieges in 1684 and 1685.
7 August 1687: the Acrocorinth is captured after the Ottoman garrison abandoned it.
28 September 1687: the Acropolis garrison capitulates.
30 September 1687: Venetian victory at Herceg Novi (the Montenegro section of the page gives '31 September', so the sources conflict).
1688: Risan, in the Bay of Kotor, is Venetian.
10 April 1688: 'Venice abandoned Athens and evacuated Attica'.
11 September 1688: Knin falls after a twelve-day siege.
12 August 1690: Monemvasia falls, 'removing the last Ottoman stronghold in the Morea'.
12 August 1690: with Monemvasia the Morea is Venetian.
26 November 1690: Vrgorac is taken (the region is the Dalmatian hinterland, my reading).
January 1699 (26 January in the infobox): the Treaty of Karlowitz.
January 1699: in Dalmatia Venice 'kept its inland gains but gave up Popovo polje, Klek, and Sutorina to keep the existing border near Ragusa'.
Spring-early summer 1715: 'the Ottoman fleet captured both islands' (no exact dates).
1715: Souda and Spinalonga 'capitulated in exchange for safe departure'.
1715: Kythira is lost (Stato da Mar: '1238-1715, 1718-1797'); the war page does not mention it.

1715: Lefkada page: 'following the Ottoman reconquest of the Morea in 1715, the Venetians initially abandoned Lefkada to focus their resources on the defence of Corfu'; Siege of Corfu page: the commander 'abandoned Lefkada after destroying its fortifications ...
25 June 1715: the Ottoman army crosses the Isthmus and the Acrocorinth surrenders; the Ottoman Empire had declared war on 9 December 1714.
20 July 1715: the Ottomans storm Nauplia.
Early October 1715 (25 June plus a hundred days, my arithmetic): the Morea is lost.
Early October 1715 (25 June plus a hundred days, my arithmetic): the reconquest of the Morea is complete 'within a hundred days' (the page gives no end date).

About November 1716: Siege of Corfu page: 'Two months later, the Venetian fleet recaptured Lefkada', after the recapture of Butrint on 2 September 1716 (the siege was lifted on 21 August 1716); Lefkada page: 'the island was reoccupied and the fortifications restored'.
1717: Venice captures Preveza and Arta; the treaty let the Ottomans keep their conquests 'except Preveza and a few forts in Herzegovina'.
1718: Kythira is Venetian again (Stato da Mar: '1238-1715, 1718-1797'); the Passarowitz terms are not in the war page.
By the end of 1796: 'by the end of 1796 the French troops were occupying the Venetian state up to the Adige River' (French forces had invaded Piedmont in spring 1796).
12 May 1797: the occupation gives way to the republic's surrender; see the dissolve event.
12 May 1797: Ludovico Manin surrenders unconditionally and the Major Council declares the end of the republic.

wars.name: Zara War and the Fourth Crusade
wars.outcome: Venice recaptured Zara (1202), besieged and helped sack Constantinople in 1204 ('which ended the Byzantine Empire'), bought Crete from Boniface of Montferrat (12 August 1204) and occupied Dyrrhachium in 1205.

wars.name: Genoese occupation of Crete under Enrico Pescatore
wars.outcome: Venice evicted Pescatore in 1212; a treaty with Genoa of 11 May 1217 left Crete 'securely under Venetian control'.

wars.name: Hungarian-Venetian war over Dalmatia (Treaty of Zadar)
wars.outcome: Treaty of Zadar, 18 February 1358: Venice gave up Dalmatia 'from the Kvarner to the Bay of Kotor' and the Dalmatia title; kept the Istrian coast and the Treviso region.

wars.name: Revolt of St. Titus
wars.outcome: Venice retook Candia on 9 May 1364; the Kallergis brothers were captured by treason in April 1367 and the revolt ended in 1368.

wars.name: War of Chioggia
wars.outcome: The war 'ended definitively on 8 August 1381 with the Treaty of Turin'.

wars.name: War of Padua
wars.outcome: Venice acquired Vicenza, Belluno and Feltre (1404) and Padua, Verona and Este (1405); Francesco Novello da Carrara was executed in 1406.

wars.name: Venetian invasion of the Patriarchate of Aquileia
wars.outcome: 'In 1420, Venice annexed the Friulian territories'; Emperor Sigismund acknowledged them in 1433.

wars.name: Ottoman-Venetian war of 1423
wars.outcome: 'The Ottomans began a seven-year sea war with Venice in 1423.'

wars.name: Venetian-Milanese wars in Lombardy
wars.outcome: Venice acquired Brescia (1426) and Bergamo (1428); the Peace of Lodi (1454) 'confirmed Bergamo and Brescia to the Republic' (History page).

wars.name: Ottoman-Venetian War (1463-1479)
wars.outcome: The Ottomans took Argos (3 April 1463), Negroponte (5 August 1470) and, by the Treaty of Constantinople of 25 January 1479, Shkodra; Venice took Imbros, Thasos and Samothrace (1466) and de facto Cyprus.

wars.name: War of Ferrara (1482-1484)
wars.outcome: Venetian victory: the Treaty of Bagnolo (7 August 1484) ceded Rovigo and a broad swath of the Po delta to Venice.

wars.name: Ottoman-Venetian war of 1499
wars.outcome: 'Venice surrendered the bases of Lepanto, Durazzo, Modon, and Coron' (main page); Venice gained Cephalonia (1500) and Ithaca (1503) per Stato da Mar.

wars.name: War of the League of Cambrai
wars.outcome: Agnadello (14 May 1509) cost Venice its fifteenth-century mainland; Padua (17 July) and Vicenza (November 1509) were recovered, Brescia lost in February 1512, and the treaties of Noyon (August 1516) and Brussels (6 December 1516) with Verona's return in…

wars.name: Ottoman-Venetian War (1570-1573)
wars.outcome: Nicosia fell on 9 September 1570 and Famagusta on 1 August 1571; the peace of 7 March 1573 made Cyprus an Ottoman province, with an indemnity of 300,000 ducats and a modified Dalmatian border.

wars.name: Uskok War
wars.outcome: Venice fought Archduke Ferdinand; the page gives no territorial result.

wars.name: Cretan War (1645-1669)
wars.outcome: Chania fell on 22 August 1645, Rethymno on 20 October 1646, Candia on 5 September 1669; Venice kept Tinos, Kythera, Spinalonga, Gramvousa and Souda and gained ground in Dalmatia (Klis, Novigrad).

wars.name: Morean War
wars.outcome: Treaty of Karlowitz, January 1699: 'Morea ceded to Venice; Venetian gains in inland Dalmatia'; Venice also kept Aegina and Kephalonia and gave up Popovo polje, Klek and Sutorina.

wars.name: Ottoman-Venetian War (1714-1718)
wars.outcome: The Ottomans retook the Morea in 1715 'within a hundred days'; the Treaty of Passarowitz (21 July 1718): 'Morea ceded back to the Ottoman Empire; some Venetian gains in Dalmatia'.

wars.name: French invasion of the Venetian state and the fall of the Republic
wars.outcome: French forces occupied the state up to the Adige by the end of 1796; preliminaries of 18 April 1797 gave the Balkan possessions to Austria and the Lombard part to France; Manin surrendered on 12 May; Campo Formio (17 October 1797) shared the territory.

certainty.note: The lagoon duchy's mainland extension is only 7 to 19 km (main page) and the Dalmatian, Aegean and Peloponnesian possessions are ports and islands whose limits no treaty fixed; the Treaty of Zadar of 1358 is the first dated frontier on the…

Port-and-island possessions and a mainland whose limits follow wars (Cambrai, Ferrara, Lodi); the Dalmatia line of 1358 and the lines of the 1516-1517 settlement are treaty lines but not described in the pages opened.

The Ottoman frontier is fixed by the treaties of Karlowitz (1699) and Passarowitz (1718); the Terraferma frontiers of the eighteenth century are not on a page opened here (taken as sharp by default, weak).
